newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Berkshire sells 3.9 pct of Tranz Rail -- brokers.
newsitem.headline: Berkshire sells 3.9 pct of Tranz Rail -- brokers.

text.p: U.S. investor Berkshire Partners has sold five million of its 21.9 million shares in New Zealand's Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd at NZ$7.50 per share, brokers said on Thursday.
The shares were on-sold to local institutions at $7.60 per share.
The deals were transacted by broker Doyle Paterson Brown, but principal Murray Doyle declined to confirm it was Berkshire which was the seller.
Tranz Rail shares were down 20 cents to $7.80 shortly after midday.
"Berkshire Partners have sold five million shares," said Ord Minnett broker Geoff Brown.
He said local institutions had been light in Tranz Rail for some time. He described the price as a "reasonable discount".
There was some surprise that Berkshire was a seller as it traditionally holds its stakes for 7-10 years.
Tranz Rail's share price has risen strongly from $6.80 on October 9 to a closing high of $8.05 on Tuesday.
Some of that rise has been attributed to its first-quarter report released at the beginning of the month.
The stock listed on June 14 and closed on its first day at $7.10 and fell to a low of $6.25 a month later.
Tranz Rail is the only operator of New Zealand's railway system.
